source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Code Correctness in LLMs via Sparse Autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE features to an LLM and reports their predictive and causal effects, while also explicitly finding that SAE features do not fully resolve polysemanticity. The latter refines claims that SAE features are clean, complete units.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses superposition and cites Toy Models of Superposition, but does not test toy-model geometry, feature sparsity or importance-dependent transitions. Rows below concern its own SAE-derived features and their measured prediction, steering, orthogonalization, or reported polysemantic behavior. Attention shifts are not included because they do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained GemmaScope SAEs as a tool to find code-correctness directions in Gemma-2-2b. It reports only how well those directions predict and steer correctness. No result bears on toy-model geometry, the capacity account, alternative origins of polysemanticity, how features spread across neurons, SAE completeness, stability or canonicity, or feature dimensionality. Its one relevant remark is a single qualitative example: one SAE latent's top logits include foreign-language tokens. That is recorded under fits_no_version rather than counted as a test of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE-derived predictor directions reliably detect incorrect code (F1 0.821) but not correct code (F1 0.504). Correct-steering fixes 4.04% of errors but corrupts 14.66% of correct code, so they advise selective steering. Orthogonalizing the correct direction shows it is necessary for generation. Successful generation depends on attending to test cases rather than problem descriptions. Base-model directions keep their effectiveness after instruction-tuning. The polysemanticity remark is a side observation, not a conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses pretrained JumpReLU SAEs, feature-selection statistics, activation steering, and weight orthogonalization on Gemma-2 code-generation representations. It does not reproduce the original toy-network experiments or their superposition geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported prediction and steering results vary by feature-selection metric and direction; the instruction-tuned model has lower reported F1 and correction rate than the base model. Temperature variation is reported to affect correct-feature detection, but exact values by temperature are not stated in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: A GemmaScope SAE latent (L19-5441) selected for error detection also shows foreign-language tokens among its top logits. The authors take this as evidence that SAEs do not fully solve polysemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents in LLMs can remain polysemantic (not fully monosemantic).

record.problems: The main experiments use one base model and one instruction-tuned model, with one selected feature per reported direction. Some control rates are not stated in the text, and some comparisons are described through figures. The paper reports limits in feature specificity and an ineffective incorrect-steering direction.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows left out. Attention redistribution is not included because it measures prompt attention, not the claim versions' representation properties.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All of it: no test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation.
All of it: no test of the non-capacity origins of polysemanticity.
All of it: SAEs are assumed to decompose superposed representations. Neither distribution of features across neurons nor recovery quality is measured.
All of it: no test of completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicity. There is only an anecdotal polysemantic latent.
All of it: 1-D decoder directions are used without comparison to multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' classification overstates the study. Superposition and SAEs appear only as motivation and tool. All quantitative rows measure the authors' code-correctness method, so no verdicts are given. Attention-shift and temperature results (F1 0.821 to 0.986) likewise do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometric arrangement is tested.
The study does not test whether capacity pressure causes neuron polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
It does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.

The study tests whether SAE-derived features in Gemma-2 can be recovered and used for code-correctness prediction and intervention. It does not measure how features are distributed across neurons, compare SAEs with other dictionaries, or establish generality beyond the tested model and code-correctness task.

The study reports examples of SAE features responding to unrelated patterns, but does not test feature stability across seeds, SAE configurations, models, or datasets, or establish whether features are canonical.
It uses decoder vectors as directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Selected the incorrect-predicting SAE feature using t-statistics and measured its prediction of code correctness.
rows.note: The paper reports reliable prediction of incorrect code using an SAE-derived feature.
rows.check: This is the F1 of the study's own selected predictor latent (a performance metric of its method). It does not measure whether models spread features across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features in the V4 sense.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Selected the correct-predicting SAE feature using t-statistics and measured its prediction of code correctness.
rows.note: The result is substantially weaker than incorrect-code prediction; the authors say formatting-related false positives limit the feature's specificity.
rows.check: This is the method's own predictor performance. Weak correct-code F1 says nothing about SAE completeness, stability or canonicity (V5), or about superposition in LLMs (V4).

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Measured precision and recall for the correct-predicting SAE feature.
rows.measure: Precision and recall for predicting correct code
rows.note: The paper attributes the low precision to false positives, including well-formatted but incorrect code.
rows.check: This is the precision and recall of the method's own predictor, not a measure of any version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Measured precision and recall for the incorrect-predicting SAE feature.
rows.measure: Precision and recall for predicting incorrect code
rows.note: The feature detects error-associated anomalies, according to the authors.
rows.check: This is the precision and recall of the method's own predictor, not a measure of any version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Added the correct-steering SAE direction to the residual stream.
rows.baseline: 0% correction for baseline with no steering
rows.note: The authors describe the correction effect as modest.
rows.check: This is a steering correction rate for the study's own direction. It is a tool-performance result, not a measure of superposition or dictionary-feature properties.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Added the correct-steering SAE direction to the residual stream.
rows.baseline: 0% corruption for baseline with no steering
rows.note: Steering changes generation but corrupts initially correct code more often than it fixes initially incorrect code.
rows.check: This is the steering corruption rate for the study's own direction, a tool-performance result.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Added a zero-discrimination control feature to the residual stream.
rows.measure: Correction and corruption compared with control
rows.value: p < 0.001 for steering versus control on correction; p = 1.0 for steering versus control on corruption
rows.note: The paper does not give the control's correction or corruption rates in the text.
rows.check: This is a control comparison for steering, given only as p-values (control rates appear only in Figure 4). It is not a measure of any version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Added the incorrect-steering SAE direction to the residual stream.
rows.value: The paper reports repeated '8' tokens and calls the direction ineffective for identifying incorrect features.
rows.note: No numerical correction or corruption rate is stated for this steering direction.
rows.check: This is a qualitative failure of the incorrect-steering direction (repeated '8' tokens). The authors attribute it to their selection metric (separation scores), not to SAE or superposition properties.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Orthogonalized writing matrices to remove the correct-steering direction.
rows.uncertainty: p < 0.001 versus baseline; p < 0.001 versus control
rows.note: The abstract gives 83.62% and 18.97%; the body rounds these to 83.6% and 19.0%. The feature's removal substantially degrades functional code.
rows.check: This is a weight-orthogonalization ablation of the method's own direction (83.62% vs 18.97% control corruption). It is causal validation of the tool, not of any version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Orthogonalized writing matrices to remove the control feature.
rows.check: This is a control value (18.97%) that serves as the baseline for r9. It should not be a separate row with the state 'partial'.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Orthogonalized writing matrices to remove the incorrect-steering direction.
rows.uncertainty: p = 0.998 versus control; p < 0.001 versus baseline
rows.note: Removing the selected direction corrected fewer errors than removing the control direction.
rows.check: This is orthogonalization of the incorrect direction: 2.2% vs 5.5% control. It reflects the failure of the selection metric and is not 'reversed' relative to any version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b instruction-tuned model
rows.operation_detail: Applied the base-model incorrect-predicting SAE feature to the instruction-tuned model.
rows.note: The SAE was trained on base-model representations; the paper says error detection remains reliable after instruction-tuning.
rows.check: This is transfer of the method's predictor to the instruction-tuned model. It concerns persistence of the tool's performance, not SAE stability as V5 means it (seeds, configurations, dictionaries).

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b instruction-tuned model
rows.operation_detail: Applied the base-model correct-steering SAE direction with the same coefficient.
rows.note: The paper reports a lower correction rate than in the base model, while describing the effect as statistically significant.
rows.check: This is the transferred steering correction rate, a tool-performance result.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Inspected the top token logit increases associated with the incorrect-predicting SAE feature.
rows.value: The feature responds to foreign-language tokens as well as error-associated anomalies.
rows.note: The authors present this as evidence that SAE decomposition does not fully solve polysemanticity.
rows.check: This is a qualitative top-logit inspection showing one latent responds to foreign-language tokens as well as error-associated anomalies. It bears on SAE latent monosemanticity, which V5 (complete/stable/canonical) does not name. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Inspected the top token logit increases and prediction errors associated with the correct-predicting SAE feature.
rows.value: The feature responds to formatting tokens; the paper reports false positives on well-formatted incorrect code.
rows.note: The authors characterize this feature as a superficial correctness signal rather than a reliable semantic indicator.
rows.check: This latent responds to formatting tokens, which makes it a poor correctness predictor. That concerns the latent's usefulness for the task, not a property named by any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Base Gemma-2-2b on MBPP, and transfer of selected features to its instruction-tuned model
reader_labels.reason: SAE-derived features predict code errors and show measurable intervention effects; selected features retain some predictive or steering effectiveness after instruction-tuning (r1, r5, r9, r12, r13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Correctness prediction and steering on the tested MBPP setup
reader_labels.reason: Correct-code prediction is weak, correct steering causes substantial corruption, and the selected incorrect-steering direction is ineffective or counterproductive when removed (r2, r6, r8, r11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The reported Gemma-2-2b correctness-predicting SAE features
reader_labels.reason: The features respond to unrelated language or formatting patterns and produce false positives, so the reported features are not fully clean, single-purpose units (r14, r15, r3).
